title: Windtunnel — Aerofoil Test Bench
description: A real lattice-Boltzmann wind tunnel: sculpt a body, watch it shed vortices, read lift and drag, sweep a polar.
concept: A D2Q9 lattice-Boltzmann solver runs a live wind tunnel in a single file. Pick one of seven bodies or paint your own solid cells with a brush, then tilt the freestream and watch the wake answer. Forces come off the body by momentum exchange at every bounce-back link, so lift and drag are measured rather than faked — the strip chart shows the lift oscillating as vortices shed, and the Strouhal readout lands near 0.23 for a cylinder. The polar sweep re-runs the whole simulation across fifteen angles of attack on a coarse grid and plots the CL and CD curves so you can find the stall knee yourself.
features: Seven body presets plus freehand sculpt and erase brushes over the lattice
NACA 4-digit aerofoil with live camber, thickness and scale controls
Measured lift and drag by momentum exchange, with a scrolling strip chart and Strouhal readout
Four fields — speed, vorticity, pressure, schlieren — across four palettes, with tracer streaks and pressure contours
Polar sweep: fifteen angles of attack re-simulated on a coarse grid, plotted as CL/CD curves with peak-lift and best-L/D callouts
Puff tool that injects momentum into the flow to trip the wake by hand
Export PNG with a measurement caption, export JSON including the polar, share a link that carries the sculpted body as RLE
Named design slots in localStorage and a window.WINDTUNNEL console handle

interaction.mouse: Drag on the tunnel to sculpt or erase solid cells; the Puff tool injects momentum along the drag.
interaction.click: Preset, field and palette chips switch body and visualisation; Run Polar sweeps the angle of attack.
interaction.touch: Full touch sculpting via pointer events; the panel stacks under the tunnel and the strip chart hides on small screens.
interaction.keyboard: Space pauses, R restarts the flow, 1–4 switch field, P runs the polar sweep.

notes: Coarse-lattice bounce-back with tunnel blockage overestimates absolute drag (a cylinder reads CD near 1.9 against about 1.1 in reality); the trends, the shedding frequency and the shape of the polar are the honest part.
